title: Watching Excel think
summary: Step through a formula with Evaluate Formula, check pieces with F9, show every formula at once, and know when Excel recalculates.
objectives: Step through a formula with Evaluate Formula, one piece at a time.
Check part of a formula with F9 in the formula bar, then Esc.
Show every formula on a sheet with Ctrl+` (Show Formulas).
Tell Automatic from Manual calculation, and recalculate with F9.

slides.h: Evaluate Formula: Excel’s working, step by step
p: **Formulas › Evaluate Formula** shows a formula being worked out one piece at a time, like a teacher writing the working on the board.
Click **Evaluate** to work out the underlined part; click again for the next one.
**Step In** opens a cell the formula points at, to see that cell’s own formula.
The best tool when a result looks wrong and you can’t see why.
In real life: billed ₹8,500 for 40 plates at ₹250 with a ₹1,500 discount. Evaluate Formula showed the client exactly how.

slides.h: F9: check one piece, then Esc
p: In the formula bar, select part of a formula and press **F9**: Excel shows that part’s value. Press **Esc** to put the formula back.
Always press **Esc** afterwards. Press Enter instead and the number replaces that part of the formula for good.
Any piece works: a range shows as {40,60,25}, a test shows TRUE or FALSE.
On many laptops you need **Fn+F9**.
In real life: suspected the target in a long formula. He selected just that part, pressed F9, saw 0 (the target cell was empty), and pressed Esc.

check.q: You select part of a formula, press F9 and see its value. What do you press next to keep the formula as it was?
check.explain: Esc cancels the edit. Enter would keep the number in place of that part.

why.0: Enter saves the number into the formula: the formula stops updating.

lecture.title: Every formula, and when Excel calculates

slides.h: Show Formulas: the whole sheet at once
p: Press **Ctrl+`** (the key above Tab) and every cell shows its formula instead of its answer. Press it again to switch back.
A typed-in number hiding among formulas stands out: it’s the one without =.
Columns widen to fit; nothing is changed. Also at **Formulas › Show Formulas**.
In Sheetah’s grids, press Ctrl+` or click the **{=}** button in the toolbar.
In real life: presses Ctrl+` first on every workbook she reviews: a total typed in by hand stands out at once.

p: Normally Excel recalculates the moment anything changes. In **Manual** mode it waits until you press **F9**.
Switch at **Formulas › Calculation Options**.
The mode comes from the first workbook you open, so a colleague’s file can switch your Excel to Manual.
Numbers that won’t update? Check the calculation mode first.
In real life: shared a huge budget saved in Manual mode. Next morning everyone’s totals looked wrong, until someone pressed F9.

terms: recalculate only when you press F9

bad.title: Manual
bad.text: You change a price and the totals don’t move. The status bar says **Calculate**. Press **F9** to recalculate.

good.title: Automatic (the default)
good.text: Every formula updates as soon as you press Enter. Keep it like this unless a huge file is very slow.

check.q: You change a number but the total beside it doesn’t change, and the status bar says Calculate. What is going on?
options: Calculation is set to Manual: press F9
check.explain: “Calculate” in the status bar means Excel is waiting for F9. Switch back with Formulas › Calculation Options › Automatic.

why.0: A wrong formula would still recalculate.
why.2: Nothing is damaged: Excel is just waiting.

demo.intro: Work out each catering bill, then look inside the formula and at every formula on the sheet.

steps.say: Fill it down for every event.
Like Evaluate Formula, fx? shows each step: B2, C2, the multiplication, then the subtraction.
Show Formulas (Ctrl+` in Excel): every cell shows its formula. They all follow the same pattern.
Press it again to see the answers.

demo.outro: Evaluate Formula, F9 and Show Formulas let you see what Excel is doing, so a wrong answer is never a mystery.

lab.intro: Finish the catering bills, then answer questions about how Excel works them out. Click **fx?** in the toolbar to see any formula worked out step by step.

tasks.prompt: In **E2**, work out the Reddy wedding’s bill: plates × rate − discount.
hints: Point at the cells: B2, C2 and D2.
Multiplication happens before subtraction, so no brackets are needed.

tasks.prompt: Fill the formula down to **E6**, so every event has its bill.
hints: Drag the fill handle (the small square) down to E6.
Each row should use its own plates, rate and discount.

tasks.prompt: Evaluate Formula works through =B3*C3-D3 for the office lunch (60 plates, ₹180, ₹900 off). Put the steps in order.
hints: It looks up cells as it reaches them.
The last step is the answer.
tasks.explain: Cells are replaced as Excel reaches them; × happens before −.

tasks.prompt: You select **B2*C2** in the formula bar of E2 and press F9. What does the formula bar show?
hints: F9 replaces only the selected part.
The rest of the formula stays.
tasks.explain: Only the selected part becomes its value: =10000-D2. Press Esc to undo it.

tasks.prompt: A colleague’s file opens and the totals don’t change when you type new numbers. What do you check first?
hints: What would make Excel stop recalculating?
tasks.explain: If it’s on Manual, switch back to Automatic, or press F9 to recalculate now.

tasks.prompt: With Show Formulas on, one cell in the bill column shows **8000** while the others show =B4*C4-D4 and so on. What does that tell you?
tasks.explain: A typed number won’t update when plates or rates change. Put the formula back.
options: Someone typed a number over the formula there
Shows every formula instead of its answer
quiz.explain: Show Formulas. Press it again to switch back.

quiz.q: In the formula bar you select part of a formula and press F9, then Enter. What happens?
options: That part is permanently replaced by its value
quiz.explain: Enter saves the edit. Use Esc after F9 to keep the formula.

quiz.q: Evaluate Formula shows =60*180-D3. What does the next click show?
quiz.explain: Multiplication is worked out before D3 is looked up for the subtraction.

quiz.q: Which calculation mode is best for everyday work?
quiz.explain: Automatic keeps every answer up to date. Manual is only for very slow, huge files.

quiz.q: What does Step In do in Evaluate Formula?
options: Shows the formula inside a cell that the formula uses
quiz.explain: Step In opens the referenced cell, so you can follow a chain of formulas.

points: **Evaluate Formula** steps through a formula one piece at a time.
**F9** in the formula bar shows a selected part’s value; always press **Esc** afterwards.
**Ctrl+`** shows every formula; numbers that won’t update usually mean **Manual** calculation.
recap.cheat: Evaluate, F9 then Esc, Ctrl+`, and keep calculation Automatic.
